payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the woman's jacket fully closed, with its actual front closure edges joined throughout and no remaining front opening?
node.criteria: Pass only when visual evidence establishes that the jacket's actual front closure edges are joined throughout the full closure and no opening remains. Fail when an identifiable opening between those edges remains at any section, even if another section is visibly closed. Compare corresponding closure-edge features across the source and edited images; distinguish the actual closure from the outer silhouette, projecting pink fabric, folds, sleeves, and bottom hem. Neither a broad pink flap nor the absence of a visible gap establishes full closure when the closure is concealed. Unknown when the closure cannot be located or traced sufficiently to establish completion, and no identifiable remaining opening establishes failure. A visible closed portion alone is insufficient for pass.
node.binding: Reference garment: the woman's pink jacket in the SOURCE image. Locate its front panel edges on either side of the visible dark central strip, following them from the neckline toward the lower front hem; the strip identifies the opening region but is not itself a fastener. Evaluation target: the corresponding front closure of that same jacket in the EDITED image. Account for the changed sideways pose: first locate the neckline below her head, distinguish the sleeve containing the visible hand from the torso panels, and locate the torso panel's lower hem above or alongside the dark trousers. Use these landmarks to search for the corresponding front edges from neckline to lower front hem, inspecting upper, middle, and lower portions without treating them as separate requirements. The large pink section projecting toward image-right is not by itself evidence of either closure or an opening; identify its relationship to the actual front edges before using it as evidence. Do not substitute a sleeve boundary, side seam, fold, outer contour, or bottom hem for the closure. Requested state: the actual front edges meet throughout, leaving no front opening. If any identifiable section remains open, fail; if no opening is identifiable but any necessary section remains concealed or untraceable, retain unknown rather than infer full closure.
